newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade sharply lower.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade sharply lower on Wednesday as a lift from overnight gains on Wall Street was cancelled out by a one-pfennig fall in the dollar against the mark from 34-month highs.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 42.41 points, or 1.29 percent, at 3,233.75 points. But no major consolidation was yet in sight as the index caught up with a sharp slide in prices in after-bourse screen trade on Tuesday.
But the IBIS DAX index, which already reflected Tuesday's late trade, was up 11.53 points at 3,244.41 points and March DTB DAX futures were up 14.5 points at 3,252 points.

"Everyone is waiting for a consolidation, and that's why it's just not coming," commented one Frankfurt dealer, who attributed the declines to a swift bout of dollar-driven profit-taking, which could be rapidly reversed.
The biggest decliners over bourse trade included insurance giant Allianz AG Holding, which ended down 83 marks at 3,240.
The insurer said earlier in the session that its 1996 pre-tax profit increased to around 4.1 billion marks, well above forecasts of between 3.45 and 3.80 billion marks.
Allianz has been a strong performer in recent weeks after several significant earnings upgrades.
In the banking sector, lately also an outperformer as its 1996 earnings season gets into full swing, prices came under some pressure.
Recent favourite Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel Bank AG, was down 1.90 marks at 50.60, after its risk provisions rose around 50 percent from year-ago levels, above expectations.
German share traders will be keeping a watchful eye on U.S. data due later, including January consumer price data.
"Wall Street is key. I believe it is due a downward correction in the coming week and if so, the DAX will follow," another dealer said.
